title: A 19-year-old in rural Vermont took the first known detailed photos of snowflakes in 1885
body: Wilson Bentley of Jericho, Vermont, was given a microscope by his mother when he was 15, and at first he tried to draw the snow crystals he saw through it. He then fixed a bellows camera to a compound microscope, caught each crystal on a blackboard and moved it quickly onto a microscope slide. On **15 January 1885** he photographed his first snowflake. Over his life he captured more than 5,000 snow crystals, and he argued that no two were alike.

slides.caption: A page of snow crystals photographed by Wilson Bentley of Jericho, Vermont, numbered 889 to 900. Every one has six sides, and every one is different.

slides.question: Bentley's 1931 book Snow Crystals was illustrated with how many of his photographs?
slides.explanation: 2,500 photographs. He wrote it with William J. Humphreys of the US Weather Bureau, and it came out shortly before his death.

events.text: Gets a microscope from his mother, aged 15
Publishes Snow Crystals and dies at his farm

slides.question: Which idea about snow did Bentley argue for?
options: No two snow crystals are alike
slides.explanation: With George Henry Perkins he published an article arguing that no two snow crystals were alike, an idea that caught the public imagination.
